Systematic Review Links Social Anxiety and Loneliness to Problematic AI Use

A systematic review synthesizing empirical literature has found that social anxiety and loneliness are generally associated with problematic artificial intelligence use among adults. As generative artificial intelligence systems become increasingly integrated into everyday life, the psychological mechanisms linked to excessive or maladaptive engagement with these tools have remained insufficiently understood. The systematic review synthesized the empirical literature examining the relationship between problematic AI use, social anxiety, and loneliness among adults.

The review included 20 empirical studies comprising a total of 15,881 adult participants identified across the Web of Science, Scopus, and PubMed databases following PRISMA 2020 guidelines. Methodological quality across the included research was evaluated using the Joanna Briggs Institute Critical Appraisal Checklist for Analytical Cross-Sectional Studies. The synthesized evidence demonstrated consistent empirical associations connecting elevated social anxiety and heightened feelings of loneliness with problematic patterns of artificial intelligence use.

Theoretical frameworks highlighted in the synthesis suggest why these psychological states may relate to intensive technology habits. Within the Interaction of Person-Affect-Cognition-Execution model and Compensatory Internet Use Theory, interacting with artificial intelligence systems is conceptualized as a potentially nonjudgmental and continuously accessible compensatory activity. However, the review noted that only four of the 20 studies evaluated social anxiety and loneliness simultaneously within the same analytical model.

Because the current evidence base relies predominantly on cross-sectional designs, the relative contributions and precise temporal ordering of social anxiety and loneliness remain unresolved. The authors emphasized that the compensatory function of artificial intelligence requires verification through rigorous longitudinal research. In addition, the researchers concluded that social anxiety and loneliness represent critical variables worth evaluating in future prevention-oriented initiatives and targeted intervention research addressing problematic AI use.

Subject of Research: Systematic review examining associations between social anxiety, loneliness, and problematic artificial intelligence use in adults

Article Title: Is AI a Compensatory Tool? A Systematic Review of Social Anxiety, Loneliness, and Problematic AI Use

Article References: Kara, B. C., Griffiths, M. D., Türk, F., & Deniz, M. E. (2026). Is AI a Compensatory Tool? A Systematic Review of Social Anxiety, Loneliness, and Problematic AI Use. International Journal of Mental Health and Addiction. https://doi.org/10.1007/s11469-026-01770-9

Keywords: artificial intelligence, problematic AI use, social anxiety, loneliness, systematic review, PRISMA 2020, mental health, adult psychology, cross-sectional studies, compensatory internet use, I-PACE model, generative AI, psychological processes, behavioral addiction, JBI appraisal, interpersonal distress

News Source: Glenn Wilkins. (November 28, 2026). Systematic Review Links Social Anxiety and Loneliness to Problematic AI Use. Scienmag.
